div.head: VI Atr 5.3
div.ab: ⁊ se ðe þæs geswican wille ⁊ clænnesse healdan, hæbbe he Godes miltse, ⁊ þær to eacan to woroldweorðscipe, þæt he sy þegenweres ⁊ þegenrihtes wyrþe ge on life ge on legere.
⁊ se ðe þæs geswican wille ⁊ clænnesse healdan, hæbbe he Godes miltse ⁊ þær to eacan, to woroldweorðscipe, þæt he sy þegenweres ⁊ þegenrihtes wyrþe, ge on life ge on legere.
And se ðe þæs geswican wille and clænnesse healdan hæbbe he Godes miltse, and þærtoeacan to woroldweorðscipe, þæt he sy þegenweres and þegenrihtes wyrþe, ge on life ge on legere.
Und wer hiervon abstehen und Keuschheit bewahren will, erhalte er Gottes Gnade und ausserdem als weltlichen Ehrenrang, dass er Thegn-Wergeldes und Thegn-Vorrechts geniesse, wie im Leben so im Grabe.

And whoever will desist from this and keep chastity, let him have God's mercy and, in addition, as a worldly honour, that he be entitled to a thegn's wergild and a thegn's rights, both in life and in the grave.

But he who will turn from marriage and observe celibacy shall obtain the favour of God, and in addition, as worldly honour, he shall enjoy the wergeld and the privileges of a thegn, both during his life and after his death.

And he who will renounce it and practice celibacy will have God’s favor, and also, as a privilege in this world, he shall be deemed worthy of a thane’s wergild and a thane’s rights, both in life and after death.
